title: The Temple Bell (മലയാളം)

full_text:
The regional Shiva temple possessed an ancient, massive bell cast of seven sacred metals, hanging high in the stone gopuram tower. It produced a deep, resonant, melodious chime that could be heard across seven villages.

Guru Paramartha and his disciples were visiting the temple during the annual festival. While the priests were conducting rituals inside the sanctum, Matti and Madayan wandered into the bell tower.

Looking up at the gleaming bronze bell, Matti was enchanted: 'Brother Madayan, look at that magnificent bell! If our ashram possessed such a bell, our Master could summon us to philosophy classes from three miles away!'

Madayan nodded with greedy ambition: 'Indeed! Our ashram needs a voice! But how can we carry away a bell that weighs three hundred pounds?'

Matti whispered: 'The rope is loose; if we untie it tonight, we can lower the bell into our cart and roll it away!'

'There is only one obstacle,' cautioned Madayan. 'The moment we touch the clapper, the bell will ring out with a deafening chime, and the temple guards will rush in and beat us to powder!'

Matti stroked his chin, pondering this acoustic dilemma. Suddenly, his face lit up with an extraordinary spark of 'genius':

'I have solved the acoustic problem, Madayan!' proclaimed the blockhead. 'Why does a bell ring? It rings because sound enters the ears of listeners! Therefore, if we plug our ears with thick wads of cotton, we will not hear the chime! And if we cannot hear the chime, the bell cannot be ringing! It is pure philosophy!'

Madayan was dazzled by this logic: 'Brilliant, Matti! Sound cannot exist if the ear is closed!'

That night, at midnight, Matti and Madayan crept into the temple tower. Each disciple took two large balls of raw cotton, soaked them in oil, and stuffed them so deeply and tightly into their ear canals that they could not hear their own breathing!

Believing they were rendered completely acoustically invisible, Matti took a heavy iron hammer and struck the bell's clapper with all his might to loosen the pivot!

'CLAAANG! DONGGGG! CLAAANG!'

The colossal, thunderous chime reverberated across the temple courtyards, rattling the windows of the town and waking three hundred sleeping citizens!

Because their ears were plugged with cotton, Matti and Madayan heard not a whisper. Matti smiled cheerfully at Madayan and struck the bell again: 'CLAAANG! CLAAANG!'

'It works, brother!' shouted Matti (though he could not hear his own voice). 'The bell is completely silent!'

Within two minutes, fifty angry temple guards, priests, and townsmen armed with lanterns, clubs, and ropes burst into the tower!

They surrounded the two thieves, waving their cudgels in furious shouts.

Seeing the shouting guards, Matti pointed to his ears with a triumphant grin: 'You cannot hear us, and we cannot hear you! The bell is silent!'

The guards did not argue about acoustics; they fell upon the two fools with their bamboo cudgels, giving them a thorough thrashing that bypassed their ears and registered directly upon their ribs!

Dragged before the village magistrate, the cotton was pulled from their ears. Guru Paramartha had to pay twenty silver rupees to ransom his acoustic philosophers from the town jail.

Returning to the ashram, the Guru gave a lecture on sound: 'Sound, my children, travels through the air to other ears, even when your own ears are stuffed with cotton! Next time, you must stuff cotton into the ears of the entire village before you strike the bell!'
moral: Closing your own ears does not silence the sound you make; self-deception hides nothing from the world. [ML]

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Temple Bell"?
options: Foolishness of book knowledge without worldly wisdom
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
quiz.hint: Consider the virtues praised in world folklore.

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
quiz.hint: Reflect upon the resolution of the story.
